newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares weak at lunch, prognosis poor.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares weak at lunch, prognosis poor.

text.p: Singapore shares were weaker at noon on Thursday and were expected to remain weak, dealers said.
"The Singapore index is drifting down and will contine to drift down later today," said a dealer with a local firm.
At 0430 GMT the index stood at 2037.20, slipping 10.69 points. Total market volume was a low 58 million shares.
Dealers said the index's downturn reflected a poor peformance of blue chips like Semabawang, which was down Singapore $0.150 at S$6.95.
Parkway Holdings Ltd, with a morning volume of 729,000 shares, fell S$0.30, winding up at S$6.60 by lunchtime.
The healthcare group's shares have been active on speculation that the company would be taken over by property giant DBS Land, which has bought a 19.2 percent stake in it.

DBS Land was the morning's most active counter with 40 million shares changing hands while banks OCBC and OUB saw both foreign and domestic share tranches dented by the impact of bonus and rights issues respectively.
OCBC foreign stood down S$3.10 at S$15.30 while domestic fell S$1.80 to S$8.00. OUB foreign dropped 55 cents to S$9.30 and domestic stock lost 35 cents to S$5.30.
